verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, aged about {petitioner_age} years, resident of {petitioner_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a petition for Restitution of Conjugal Rights under S.9 HMA (or S.22 SMA, as selected).
Plead valid marriage with date, place and ceremonies appropriate to governing statute.
Plead cohabitation period and matrimonial home(s).
Plead specifically: date on which respondent withdrew from the society of petitioner, and the circumstances.

Plead in detail why respondent has NO reasonable excuse for withdrawal. Under the Explanation to S.9 HMA, where a question arises as to reasonable excuse, the burden lies on the person who has withdrawn — but petitioner must still plead non-existence of reasonable excuse.
Plead efforts at reconciliation: visits, communications, intervention of family/community elders.
Plead petitioner's continuing willingness and readiness to receive respondent and resume cohabitation.
Address Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha (1984) 4 SCC 90 — RCR constitutionality upheld; remedy is consortium not coercion.
Note in instructions to advocate (not in petition body): non-compliance with RCR decree for 1+ year is itself a ground for divorce under S.13(1A)(ii) HMA / S.27(2) SMA.
Tone should be conciliatory — RCR is restorative, not punitive.

sections.description: Restitution of conjugal rights — court may decree restitution where spouse has, without reasonable excuse, withdrawn from society of the other; Explanation places burden of proving reasonable excuse on withdrawing spouse
Non-compliance with RCR decree for 1 year is independent ground for divorce
Restitution of conjugal rights — analogous to S.9 HMA
Non-compliance with RCR decree for 1 year — ground for divorce under SMA
